mcNarrative: Across 100 simulated futures with varying weekly demand, the baseline average fill rate was about 89.7%, meaning roughly 1 in 10 orders would normally go unfilled even in good times. When the 78% shipping capacity cut was applied, the average fill rate dropped to about 68.8%, a decline of roughly 21 percentage points, so about 1 in 5 orders would go unfilled each week. The range of likely outcomes was wide, with the worst‑case 1‑in‑20 outcome (p5) at about 65% and the best‑case 1‑in‑20 outcome (p95) at about 72%, meaning that even in the most favorable simulated scenario, fill rates would still fall well below the 95% service target.
headline: A 78% cut to weekly shipping capacity at the China‑to‑India cell‑to‑assembly link drove the average fill rate down from about 90% to about 69%, meaning that over 1 in 3 orders would go unfilled each week during the disruption.
story: Extraction stages in Chile and China operated at or near full capacity both before and during the disruption, so the bottleneck did not originate at the mine or refining step. Precursor manufacturing in China saw its fill rate improve slightly from about 90% to about 98%, a modest gain that did not offset downstream shortfalls. The Assembly stage in Gujarat, India, was the hardest hit, with its fill rate plummeting from about 78% to about 53%, a drop of roughly 25 percentage points, meaning that roughly 1 in 2 orders would go unfilled at that stage during the tightest week (week 3). The OEM stage in Rajasthan followed a similar pattern, declining from about 91% to about 70% fill rate, with the tightest pressure occurring in week 23. Throughout the chain, the recycling stage remained idle with a 0% fill rate, so no reclaimed material was available to cushion the shortage.
risk: Running 100 Monte Carlo trials revealed that the worst‑case 1‑in‑20 outcome (p5) for the fill rate was about 65%, meaning that in a single unlucky but plausible simulation run, roughly 1 in 3 orders could go unfilled each week; if that worst case materialized, the backlog of unmet demand would swell to over 2.9 million units, far exceeding the typical weekly volume.
regional: All seven Indian regions tracked in the model finished with fill rates between about 67.7% and 68.6%, well below the 95% service level target, and every single one was classified as red status; this means that residents in Jaipur, Jodhpur, Udaipur, Ajmer, Bikaner, Kota, and Alwar would each face roughly 1 in 3 weeks of unmet demand for lithium‑ion battery packs during the disruption.
